# pve_storage_zfspool (Data Source)

Reads a ZFS pool storage configuration (`/storage/{storage}` with type `zfspool`). Reading a storage whose upstream type is not `zfspool` fails with a diagnostic naming both types.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Copyright (c) HashiCorp, Inc.

data "pve_storage_zfspool" "zfspool" {
  id = "zfspool"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) The storage identifier to read.

### Read-Only

- `blocksize` (String) ZFS block size: a power of 2 with an optional `k` or `m` suffix, for example `16k`.
- `bwlimit` (String) I/O bandwidth limit property string in KiB/s, for example `default=500,restore=100`. Keys: `clone`, `default`, `migration`, `move`, `restore`.
- `content` (Set of String) Allowed content types. Accepted values for this storage type: `images`, `rootdir`. PVE validates the set upstream.
- `disable` (Boolean) Flag to disable the storage.
- `max_protected_backups` (Number) Maximal number of protected backups per guest; `-1` means unlimited (PVE default: unlimited for users with `Datastore.Allocate`, `5` for other users).
- `nodes` (Set of String) List of nodes for which the storage configuration applies.
- `pool` (String) ZFS pool name.
- `prune_backups` (Attributes) Backup retention options overriding a backup job's settings. `keep_all = true` conflicts with the other options. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--prune_backups))
- `shared` (Boolean) Indicate that this is a single storage with the same contents on all nodes (or all listed in `nodes`). It will not make the contents of a local storage automatically accessible to other nodes; it just marks an already shared storage as such.
- `sparse` (Boolean) Use sparse volumes.

<a id="nestedatt--prune_backups"></a>
### Nested Schema for `prune_backups`

Read-Only:

- `keep_all` (Boolean) Keep all backups; conflicts with the other options.
- `keep_daily` (Number) Keep backups for the last N days.
- `keep_hourly` (Number) Keep backups for the last N hours.
- `keep_last` (Number) Keep the last N backups.
- `keep_monthly` (Number) Keep backups for the last N months.
- `keep_weekly` (Number) Keep backups for the last N weeks.
- `keep_yearly` (Number) Keep backups for the last N years.
